_about: The 37 test scenarios from the design's test plan (docs/design/HARSLL-n8n-design.md, revision 3), with the spreadsheet rows they use and the results expected with the default settings. Made-up data only. The spreadsheets in test-data/spreadsheets/ are generated from this file by scripts/make-test-spreadsheets.mjs; scripts/run-tests.mjs runs the groups and compares the results. See docs/testing.md.

reasonTexts.DATES_INVALID: The dates on the spreadsheet row are wrong or missing
reasonTexts.DEATH_REFERRED: The tenancy ended because the tenant died; these are passed to staff
reasonTexts.CHANGE_REASON_NOT_VALID: The reason for the change is not one the automation handles
reasonTexts.SAME_TENANCY_AS_EARLIER_ROW: Covered by an earlier row for the same tenancy
reasonTexts.EARLIER_ROW_NOT_COMPLETED: The earlier row for this tenancy was not completed, so this person was not added
reasonTexts.NO_ACCOUNT_REF: The row has no account reference
reasonTexts.ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND: The account could not be found in RBIS
reasonTexts.NO_START_DATE: RBIS has no start date to compare against
reasonTexts.CHECK_DATES: The dates in RBIS do not match the spreadsheet
reasonTexts.LEAVER_NOT_LIABLE: The person leaving is not the liable person in RBIS
reasonTexts.NO_OPTION_TO_TERMINATE: RBIS does not allow the current liability to be ended
reasonTexts.UNABLE_TO_ADD_PARTY: A person could not be added to the account
reasonTexts.NO_CONTACT_DETAILS: Liability started, but there were no contact details to record
reasonTexts.RBIS_ERROR: RBIS did not respond or returned an error
reasonTexts.PROCESSING_STOPPED: Processing stopped unexpectedly and the tries ran out

scenarios.title: Move-in, landlord liable, contact details
scenarios.path: Check 1 pass → check 2 single row → check 3 found → check 4 move-in, landlord liable → check 5 can end → Moved in

scenarios.title: Move-in, two joint tenants on two rows
scenarios.path: Lead row: Moved in for both people. Joint row: check 1 pass → check 2 joint row, lead updated → duplicate
scenarios.notes: The joint row is the last row of the file, not next to its lead row: the design links matching rows wherever they are.

scenarios.title: Move-in, nobody has contact details
scenarios.path: Checks pass → Moved in, call 4 skipped → updated with follow-up NO_CONTACT_DETAILS

scenarios.title: Move-out, forwarding address
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-out, landlord not liable, leaver liable → check 5 can end → Moved out, forwarding address known
scenarios.notes: The row also has the tenancy start date and contact details. Neither changes the move-out path: no contact call is expected.

scenarios.title: Move-out, no forwarding address
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-out, leaver liable → check 5 can end → Moved out, no forwarding address
scenarios.notes: Also checks tidying: the change reason is lower case, the account reference is lower case with spaces, the name has a trailing space, and the date is dd/MM/yyyy text.

scenarios.title: Move-out and move-in at the same address in one file
scenarios.path: Move-out: Moved out, no forwarding address. Then move-in: check 4 landlord liable → Moved in
scenarios.notes: Both rows have the same date, and the move-in is the earlier row in the file, so only the rule 'move-outs before move-ins on the same date' runs them in the right order. The landlord is liable for no days (from and to 1 November); that is what the default settings give.

scenarios.title: Impossible date
scenarios.path: Check 1 (a): the date is not real → refer
scenarios.notes: The impossible date stays as text in the Cases table, and in the case key.

scenarios.title: End date before start date
scenarios.path: Check 1 (a): end date before start date → refer

scenarios.title: Unknown change reason
scenarios.path: Check 1 (c): change reason not allowed → refer
scenarios.notes: Both dates are real and in order, so only test (c) can stop the row. The relevant date of a change reason other than TENANCY_START is the end date (interfaces, Keys).

scenarios.title: Death
scenarios.path: Check 1 (b): death, deathHandling refer → refer before the allowed-reasons test

scenarios.title: Joint tenants, lead row referred
scenarios.path: Lead row: check 4 move-in, a tenant liable from another date → CHECK_DATES. Joint row: check 2, lead referred → EARLIER_ROW_NOT_COMPLETED

scenarios.title: No account reference
scenarios.path: Check 3: no account reference → refer

scenarios.title: Account not in RBIS
scenarios.path: Check 3: the reference is not in RBIS, or its address does not match → refer
scenarios.notes: Two rows: AC999999 does not exist; AC100013 exists but the row's address does not match it (13b, from the account's note).

scenarios.title: Move-in, tenant already liable from the same date
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-in, landlord not liable → start date present and equal to the row's start date → ACCOUNT_ALREADY_PROCESSED

scenarios.title: Move-in, tenant already liable from another date
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-in, landlord not liable → start date differs → CHECK_DATES

scenarios.title: Move-out, landlord already liable from the end date
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-out, landlord liable → start date equals the row's end date → ACCOUNT_ALREADY_PROCESSED

scenarios.title: Move-out, landlord already liable from another date
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-out, landlord liable → start date differs → CHECK_DATES

scenarios.title: Current liability has no start date
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-out, landlord liable → RBIS has no start date → NO_START_DATE
scenarios.notes: A move-out, because a move-in with the landlord liable passes check 4 without any date test.

scenarios.title: Move-out, someone else is liable
scenarios.path: Check 4 move-out, landlord not liable → leaver is not one of the liable people → LEAVER_NOT_LIABLE (confirmLeaverIsLiable on)

scenarios.title: RBIS will not allow ending the liability
scenarios.path: Check 4 pass (leaver liable) → check 5: no option to terminate → NO_OPTION_TO_TERMINATE

scenarios.title: A joint tenant cannot be added
scenarios.path: Lead row: Moved in; landlord ended, lead tenant added, RBIS refuses the joint tenant → UNABLE_TO_ADD_PARTY, urgent. Joint row: lead referred → EARLIER_ROW_NOT_COMPLETED

scenarios.title: Landlord ended, then the lead tenant cannot be added
scenarios.path: Moved in; landlord ended, RBIS refuses the lead tenant → UNABLE_TO_ADD_PARTY, urgent
scenarios.notes: Also checks the main file's worklist (urgent cases first) and summary email (counts, the urgent line, no names or addresses).

scenarios.title: Outage before any RBIS call
scenarios.path: First try: the first RBIS call fails → failed, RBIS_ERROR, nothing changed. Automatic retry: checks run again → Moved in
scenarios.notes: The outage covers reads too (includeReads), so even the account lookup fails. It recovers after one failed call. The try count shows the failed try.

scenarios.title: Outage after the first RBIS call
scenarios.path: First try: landlord ended, then adding the tenant fails → failed, stepsDone kept. Retry: carries on from the tenant, checks skipped → updated

scenarios.title: RBIS makes a change but the reply is lost
scenarios.path: First try: tenant ended; RBIS makes the landlord liable but the reply is lost → failed. Retry: carries on at the landlord, the adapter sees it is already done → updated
scenarios.notes: The lost reply is on the second change, not the first. If the reply to the FIRST change were lost, stepsDone would be empty, the retry would run the checks again and check 4 would misread the half-changed account (see docs/build-notes/track-C.md, ambiguity A1).

scenarios.title: A case that fails on every try
scenarios.path: Every try: the first RBIS call fails → failed. After 3 tries it stays failed and is not tried again
scenarios.notes: Not urgent: no RBIS call succeeded. Listed in the worklist (failed with no tries left) and in the summary.

scenarios.title: Move-out fails once; move-in for the same account in the same file
scenarios.path: Move-out: ending the tenant's liability fails → failed; the move-in waits. Retry: move-out updated, then the move-in → updated
scenarios.notes: The move-in is never tried before the move-out is finished, so it ends with 1 try. Tried early, check 4 would have referred it as CHECK_DATES.

scenarios.title: Same file dropped twice
scenarios.path: First drop: Moved in. Second drop: the case key exists as updated → skipped

scenarios.title: Referred row sent again after RBIS data is corrected
scenarios.path: First file: account not in RBIS → ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND. Account added. Second file, same row: reopened in the new batch → Moved in

scenarios.title: File missing a required column; empty file
scenarios.path: Required columns present and at least one row? No → moved to rejected, team emailed the reason
scenarios.notes: Two files. The rows name AC100030, which is not in RBIS: if a row became a case by mistake, it would show.

scenarios.title: File that cannot be read
scenarios.path: Can the file be read? No → left for the next run, twice → third try: moved to rejected, one email

scenarios.title: File with an unsafe name
scenarios.path: File name safe? No → left in place, team emailed once to rename it; no command run on it
scenarios.notes: The group runs the Dispatcher at least twice after the drop, so 'once' is tested. The rows name AC100032, which is not in RBIS.

scenarios.title: File still being copied; Excel temporary file
scenarios.path: List .xlsx files unchanged for a minute, ignoring Excel temporary files: the new file is skipped until it has settled; the temporary file is never read
scenarios.notes: A run started while copying.xlsx is less than a minute old must not read it. The temporary file gets no batch and no email.

scenarios.title: Two files dropped together
scenarios.path: Both files taken in by one run; each case processed once
scenarios.notes: Dropped with the other files of the main group, so six files arrive together. The second file's name has brackets and a space, which the safe-name rule allows.

scenarios.title: Two runs started at the same moment
scenarios.path: Two runs race for the lock: one takes it and processes the file; the other ends

scenarios.title: File dropped while n8n is stopped
scenarios.path: n8n stopped, file dropped, n8n started → the timer (or the file trigger on start-up) finds the file → Moved in
scenarios.notes: Slow: up to 15 minutes for the timer. Stops and starts the n8n container, so it runs only with --include-slow and only in the production profile.

scenarios.title: Dates as text, as Excel dates and as Excel numbers
scenarios.path: Tidy rows: three forms of 1 November 2026 → all stored as 2026-11-01 → Moved in
